$comment: Which files are the GJC engine, and which files merely share its name prefix.
This is the manifest the extraction follows and the list eslint enforces, so
the boundary that is checked and the boundary that moves cannot drift apart.
A `server/gjc-*` file missing from both lists fails `npm test`: a new file in
the engine's namespace is a decision about what ships closed, and it should
not be possible to make it by accident.
`native/` and `src-tauri/` move wholesale and need no per-file list.

application.server/gjc-worker-client.ts: The application's end of the worker protocol. It runs in the application's process, uses application services, and stays behind when the engine moves.
application.server/gjc-engine-manifest.json: This file. It describes the split for both repositories and belongs to neither exclusively.
application.server/gjc-engine-manifest.test.ts: Keeps this manifest honest against the tree. It describes the split rather than either side of it.
application.server/gjc-live-session-root.test.ts: Asserts where the application looks for live session transcripts, not how the engine writes them.
application.server/gjc-transcript-turns.contract.bun: Checks the application's turn normalization against records written by the pinned SDK; its provider imports remain with the application.
application.server/gjc-worker-protocol-spec.test.ts: Checks the published protocol specification against the codec. Travels with whichever repository publishes the specification; listed here so the choice is deliberate.
